title: JDBC Data Access
description: The bridge from SQL to Java on the F23 JDBC data access day: connecting a Java program to PostgreSQL through pgJDBC with settings from environment variables, reading rows through the ResultSet cursor into Java objects, prepared statements and SQL injection, transactions and ACID with commit and rollback, swapping the in-memory repository for a JDBC one with try-with-resources, and testing a repository against a throwaway test database. Each page is an interactive, simulated rehearsal of a step in the F23 project; no page runs Java, JDBC or a database.
sourceCoverageNotes: Captain direction 2026-11-09 (limited scope addition approved): JDBC cannot be project work only; an interactive module that mimics the project work establishes the break from SQL to the Java connection, and the JDBC HTML pages and GIFT banks must be built. This module is that bounded addition; it is counted separately from the original course topic baseline and is not part of the 55-page visual migration, so it takes the full education and SME critic profile.

Each topic takes one F23 'JDBC data access' calendar row (/tracks/0/weeks/4/days/2, rows 0-4) with relation shared: the same rows stay mapped to the canonical project brief reporting-indexes-and-review/jdbc-data-access-project, which keeps the project lab. Topic ids and titles follow the calendar row text; the Reading row 2 is the reading-kind topic transactions-and-acid.

Concepts reused, not invented: the brief-instruction concepts the intake assigned to jdbc-data-access-project (pgJDBC and DriverManager, PreparedStatement and SQL injection, transactions and ACID, swapping the repository behind its interface, testing against a created and dropped test database) and the jdbc-review retrieval objectives o1-o3. The project brief and lab stay the place learners build the real JDBC repository; these pages rehearse each step with simulated output and do not contain the project's solution.

Module placement: after crud-aggregates-and-joins and before reporting-indexes-and-review, because the F23 project brief and the F24 JDBC review in reporting-indexes-and-review depend on these pages, and these pages depend only on F19-F20 SQL topics and the Java course. Calendar day mapping stays F23: every topic carries calendarDayIds for F23, so the delivered calendar order stays F22 then F23 then F24, and the reporting-indexes-and-review module, which spans F22 to F24, is not split; moduleOrder is the structural catalog grouping, not a reordering of calendar days.

Time: the F23 Project day is 120 minutes (Warm-up 5, Plan the work 10, Build 80, Timed without AI 15, Commit and walkthrough note 10). Resolved schedule (captain decision 2026-11-09, option A): these five pages use 52 Build minutes and the project brief 15; the project lab starts in the remaining 13 Build minutes and continues in F24's existing 25-minute Practice without AI block, one 38-minute lab with no added course time or homework.
